meters.label: Credit for 20 mentions of one word

frames.narration: A shopper searches for "cheap laptop battery". The index finds 8 pages that contain at least one of the words. Now they must be put in order.
First attempt: add up the word counts. A page whose author wrote "laptop" 14 times scores 15. The real best match, with all three words once, scores 3. Repetition wins.

Add idf. Each match is multiplied by how rare the word is, so "cheap" (in 3 pages) counts for more than "battery" (in 4). It helps with common words like "the", but counts still grow in a straight line, and the stuffed page still wins with 13.16.

Add saturation. The weight of a word is tf x (k1 + 1) / (tf + k1). With k1 = 1.2, one mention is 1.00, ten are 1.96, twenty are 2.08. The curve flattens below 2.20, so fourteen repeats are worth about twice one mention.

Add length normalization. A page longer than the average of about 12 words gets less credit per word (b = 0.75). The stuffed page scores 1.44 and drops to number 3. Document 2, with all three words, wins with 2.06.

Break it: set b to 0 and the length correction is gone. The stuffed page climbs back to number 2 with 1.60. Set b to 1 and the 2-word page "cheap laptop" takes first place with 2.34, so full correction over-rewards tiny pages.

The shopper sees the top results: the page with all three words first, then the short exact match. Scores only order results within this one query, and k1 and b should be tuned against judged queries, not by looking at a few examples.
